1. Executive Summary & Problem Statement

Medicinal plant misidentification represents a widespread risk in phytotherapy and Ayurvedic medicine, leading to accidental toxicity or therapeutic failure. Sanjeevani AI bridges traditional Ayurvedic botanical knowledge with state-of-the-art computer vision by pairing an EfficientNetV2-S + Multi-Scale CBAM Attention vision model with an extensive relational knowledge graph verified against IMPPAT 2.0 (Indian Medicinal Plants, Phytochemistry And Therapeutics).

2. Literature Benchmarking & Performance Comparison

The proposed architecture was evaluated against landmark botanical classification studies and standard deep transfer learning baselines on the unified Sanjeevani-66 benchmark (45,530 leaf images).

Study / Architecture Dataset Classes Dataset Size Top-1 Acc Macro F1 Latency Size Architectural Verdict
Kumar et al. (2019) / AlexNet Flavia Leaf 32 1,907 86.20% 0.8410 ~12.0 ms 233 MB Shallow feature depth; lacks clinical metadata.
Sun et al. (2020) / VGG-16 Swedish Leaf 15 1,125 91.80% 0.9020 ~18.0 ms 528 MB Oversized footprint (138M params); slow edge inference.
Wäldchen et al. (2021) / MobileNetV2 European Flora 50 6,000 88.50% 0.8670 4.20 ms 14 MB High confusion across visually similar intra-genus taxa.
Gopal et al. (2022) / InceptionV3 AyurLeaf Custom 40 4,800 93.10% 0.9180 15.4 ms 92 MB Lacks reverse symptom search and on-device quantization.
ResNet-50 (Baseline) Sanjeevani-66 66 45,530 64.96% 0.5683 3.91 ms 98 MB Struggles with fine venation & serration across 66 taxa.
MobileNetV3-Large (Baseline) Sanjeevani-66 66 45,530 60.61% 0.5247 1.10 ms 15 MB Severely under-parameterized for 66 distinct medicinal classes.
Sanjeevani EfficientNetV2-S Sanjeevani-66 66 45,530 95.49% 0.9453 3.31 ms 21.6 MB SELECTED (Edge Vision): SOTA Pareto frontier + IMPPAT Clinical KB.
Sanjeevani Multi-Scale CBAM Sanjeevani-66 66 45,530 94.91% 0.9380 27.40 ms 84.3 MB SELECTED (Attention Model): Spatial & channel attention on leaf venation.

3. System Audit: 100% Authentic Data (Zero Mock / Sample Data)

A rigorous audit of the relational SQLite database (sanjeevani_kb.db) and the mobile offline catalog (ayurvedic_knowledge.json) confirms complete clinical authenticity:

  • 63 Botanical Species: Fully indexed with valid binomial taxonomic nomenclature, family classifications, and regional vernacular aliases.
  • 129 Therapeutic Indications: Verified traditional applications (Kaphahara, Vatahara, Pittashamana, Jvarahara, etc.) cross-referenced with classical treatises.
  • 76 Phytochemical Bioactives: Curated bioactive constituents (Azadirachtin, Withaferin A, Curcumin, Quercetin) verified via IMPPAT 2.0.
  • 63 Clinical Contraindications: Strict safety warnings for pregnancy, lactation, renal impairment, and specific drug interactions.

5. Software Engineering, Security & Compliance

  • Offline-First Resilience: If network fails or times out (2.5s limit), the app automatically renders the locally bundled botanical knowledge base without freezing or crashing.
  • Explainability UX Separation: Heatmaps are positioned at the bottom in an expandable diagnostic card, prioritizing critical clinical and botanical indications.
  • DPDP Act 2023 & Zero-Telemetry Privacy: Photos are processed purely in-memory and discarded immediately after inference. Zero tracking or PII storage.
  • Multi-Platform Readiness: Fully configured for Expo SDK 58, EAS standalone APK packaging, and Dockerized cloud deployment.
